topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the final lecture and outlines its learning objectives on cancer therapies and modes of action.

topics.label: Traditional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities for treating cancer, including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents, along with associated systemic toxicities and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer-specific vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic strategies designed to exploit inherent tumor vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair pathway defects.

topics.label: Targeted therapies with kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the rationale, mechanisms, and clinical challenges of targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases, including off-target effects, bypass pathways, and acquired resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and cancer immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss strategies that engage immune mechanisms or antibody targeting to eliminate cancer cells, spanning monoclonal antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and engineered T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate overarching clinical challenges, epidemiological trends, future paradigms such as personalized genomics, and ethical dilemmas in treating cancer.
